title: Academic writing 2: structuring an argument
about: Collocations for organising and backing up an argument in an essay or report, such as fall into categories, raise questions, lend support to a view, put forward an argument and draw a conclusion.

parts.title: More collocations for referring to arguments

items.pattern: sth falls into two / three / several (main) categories / groups · sth is divided into categories
items.meaning: can be divided into a number of types or groups
items.example: Complaints about the local bus service **fall into three main categories**: delays, prices and dirty seats.
more: Most of the food we throw away **falls into two groups**: bread and fresh fruit.
People's reasons for moving to the countryside usually **fall into a few categories**: space, peace and cheaper houses.
items.watchOut: «Поділяються на дві категорії» — fall into two categories або are divided into two categories, а не divide on чи share into. Прийменник — into. Fall тут не «падати», а «належати до групи»: fall – fell – fallen.

items.pattern: draw / make a distinction between A and B · a clear / sharp distinction
items.meaning: show clearly that two things are different and should not be confused
items.example: The leaflet **draws a clear distinction between** food that is past its 'best before' date and food that is unsafe to eat.
more: It's important to **draw a distinction between** feeling tired and being ill.
My essay **makes a distinction between** fast food and cheap food: they aren't the same thing.
items.watchOut: «Провести межу між» — draw (або make) a distinction between. Conduct a difference — калька, а draw a difference звучить неприродно. Make a difference — зовсім інше: «мати значення, вплинути». У розмові «розрізняти» — tell the difference between.

items.pattern: take sth into consideration · take into consideration + a long object (the fact that…) · also take sth into account
items.meaning: think about something when you judge a situation or make a decision
items.example: When you compare train and bus fares, **take into consideration** how long each journey takes.
more: The council didn't **take** the needs of older people **into consideration** when it closed the post office.
The judges **took** the children's ages **into consideration** when they marked the paintings.
items.watchOut: «Брати до уваги» — take into consideration або take into account, а не take into attention: attention тут не підходить. Дієслово — take, а не draw чи put. Короткий додаток стоїть посередині (take it / the weather into consideration), а довгий можна поставити в кінець (take into consideration the fact that…).

items.pattern: make (a) reference to sb/sth · make no reference to sth · also refer to sth
items.meaning: mention something or someone, often another writer's work
items.example: In the second part of my essay, I will **make reference to** a recent survey of hospital patients.
more: The report **makes no reference to** the cost of the new cycle lanes.
In her speech, the head teacher **made reference to** last year's exam results.
items.watchOut: «Посилатися на» — make reference to або refer to, а не give / do reference to. Прийменник — to, а не on. A reference без to — ще й рекомендація від роботодавця: give sb a reference — дати комусь рекомендацію.

items.pattern: raise (important / serious) questions about sth · also raise an issue / a problem / doubts
items.meaning: make people think about questions that need an answer
items.example: The rise in bus fares **raises important questions about** who can afford to travel to work.
more: All the empty shops on the high street **raise questions about** the future of our town centre.
The new rules for dog owners **raise a few questions**: where exactly can we walk them now?
items.watchOut: Порушувати питання — raise questions. Rise (підніматися) і arise (виникати) не мають додатка: prices rise, a problem arises. Ask a question — поставити конкретне запитання людині, а raise questions — змусити людей замислитися.

items.pattern: touch on / upon an issue / a subject / a topic · touch briefly on sth
items.meaning: mention a subject briefly without discussing it in detail
items.example: The talk was mainly about school meals, but it also **touched on issues** such as sugar in drinks.
more: My essay only **touches on** the cost of recycling: the main focus is how families sort their rubbish.
In the last chapter, the writer **touches briefly on** the problem of noise from the airport.
items.watchOut: «Торкнутися теми» — зазвичай touch on (upon) a subject, з прийменником on. Touch on — згадати коротко, а не розглянути детально. Issue тут — питання, проблема, а не номер журналу.

items.pattern: make a (strong / good / convincing) case for sth / for doing sth · make the case that… · make a case against sth
items.meaning: give reasons why something is right or should happen
items.example: The article **makes a strong case for** free bus travel for students.
more: My daughter **made a good case for** getting a dog: she even promised to walk it every morning.
Local shop owners **made a case for** keeping the market open on Sundays.
items.watchOut: Case тут — сукупність аргументів, а не «випадок» чи «справа». Дієслово — make, а не do: do a case — помилка. На користь — for, проти — against.

items.pattern: assess / evaluate the significance of sth (in / for sth)
items.meaning: judge how important something is
items.example: The study tries to **assess the significance of** sleep in how well teenagers do at school.
more: It's too early to **assess the significance of** the new bypass for local shops.
The survey **assessed the significance of** price when families choose a holiday.
items.watchOut: Significance — значення в сенсі «важливість», а meaning — значення слова чи знаку: the meaning of a word, але the significance of diet. «Оцінити» тут — assess /əˈses/ або evaluate, а не value: value — цінувати.

items.pattern: lay / place / put (great / particular) emphasis on sth · lay – laid – laid
items.meaning: show that you think something is especially important
items.example: The new school menu **lays emphasis on** fresh vegetables and less sugar.
more: Our driving instructor **laid great emphasis on** checking the mirrors.
The new museum **puts** a lot of **emphasis on** hands-on activities for children.
items.watchOut: «Робити наголос на» — lay / place / put emphasis on, а не make emphasis чи do an accent. Прийменник — on. Дієслово emphasise вживають без on: emphasise the need. Наголос у слові — на першому складі: /ˈemfəsɪs/.

items.pattern: lend support / weight to a view / an argument / an idea · lend (your) support to sb / a campaign · lend – lent – lent
items.meaning: help to show that a view or argument is right; also, publicly support someone or something
items.example: The long queues at the doctor's **lend support to** the view that our town needs a second health centre.
more: The latest figures **lend support to** the idea that more people are cycling to work.
Several famous chefs have **lent their support to** the campaign for healthier school meals.
items.watchOut: Lend тут не «позичати», а «надавати»: lend support to — підкріплювати думку. Не make support to: так не кажуть. Минулий час — lent, а не lended.

items.pattern: hold firmly to the belief / view that… · hold firmly to your principles · also firmly believe that…
items.meaning: continue to believe something strongly, even when others disagree
items.example: My grandmother **holds firmly to the belief** that fresh air cures everything.
more: Some parents **hold firmly to the view** that children shouldn't get pocket money.
The old fisherman **held firmly to the belief** that the sea was getting warmer long before the scientists said so.
items.watchOut: «Твердо дотримуватися думки» — hold firmly to a belief або stick to a belief, а не keep firmly to: keep to зазвичай про правила, маршрут чи план. У розмові простіше: I firmly believe that…

items.pattern: draw an analogy between A and B · draw / make an analogy with sth
items.meaning: compare two things that are alike in some way, to help explain an idea
items.example: Our teacher **drew an analogy between** saving money and filling a bath: even a small leak empties it in the end.
more: The report **draws an analogy between** a busy airport and a beehive.
You can **draw an analogy between** learning a language and getting fit: little and often works best.
items.watchOut: «Проводити аналогію» — draw an analogy, а не conduct / carry out an analogy. Так само draw parallels і draw a distinction. Наголос — на другому складі: /əˈnælədʒi/.

items.pattern: draw parallels / a parallel between A and B · draw a parallel with sth
items.meaning: say that two things are very similar
items.example: The documentary **draws parallels between** the housing problems of the 1950s and those of today.
more: Mum likes to **draw parallels between** my teenage years and her own, usually to win an argument.
Journalists **drew parallels between** this summer's floods and those of 2007.
items.watchOut: «Проводити паралелі» — draw parallels, а не conduct parallels. Правопис: parallel — подвійне l посередині й одне в кінці.

items.pattern: present the case for / against sth · present a case / an argument
items.meaning: explain clearly and in order the reasons for something
items.example: The first half of the radio programme **presents the case for** a car-free town centre; the second half presents the case against.
more: At the meeting, two mums **presented the case for** a longer lunch break.
A good essay **presents the case for** and against before giving the writer's own view.
items.watchOut: Present тут — дієслово з наголосом на другому складі: /prɪˈzent/. Іменник «подарунок» — /ˈpreznt/. Не show the case: show так не вживають.

items.pattern: put forward an argument / an idea / a view / a plan · put an argument forward · put forward the argument that…
items.meaning: state an argument or idea so that people can discuss it
items.example: Some parents **put forward the argument that** homework should be banned in primary schools.
more: Nobody at the meeting **put forward** a better **idea**, so we booked the cheaper hotel.
The minister **put forward the argument that** a tax on sugary drinks would improve children's health.
items.watchOut: «Висувати аргумент» — put forward an argument, а не get forward чи move forward. Put – put – put: у минулому часі форма та сама. Argument тут — довід, а не сварка.

items.pattern: take (up) / adopt a position (on sth) · take up / adopt the position that… · a clear / neutral position
items.meaning: decide on an opinion about an issue and make it known
items.example: The council has **adopted the position that** drivers should pay to enter the city centre.
more: In my essay, I **take up the position that** school uniforms do more good than harm.
Most of the parents **adopted a neutral position** on the new timetable.
items.watchOut: «Займати позицію» — take up або adopt a position, а не occupy a position: це «обіймати посаду». Не плутай adopt /əˈdɒpt/ (прийняти) з adapt /əˈdæpt/ (пристосувати). Take in a position — помилка.

items.pattern: state your opinion / view / position · state (clearly / openly) that… · also give / express your opinion
items.meaning: say clearly and formally what you think
items.example: In the final paragraph, **state your opinion** clearly and give one strong reason for it.
more: Each resident had two minutes to **state their opinion** about the new bus timetable.
The head teacher **stated her opinion** very clearly: no phones in class.
items.watchOut: «Висловити думку» — state / give / express your opinion, а не tell your opinion; say your opinion теж звучить неприродно. State звучить офіційно: це слово для письма та зборів. In my opinion — однина, без -s.

items.pattern: argue convincingly / persuasively that… / for sth · a convincing argument
items.meaning: give reasons in a way that makes people believe you are right
items.example: In her letter to the council, she **argues convincingly that** the park needs better lighting.
more: My son **argued convincingly for** a later bedtime at weekends, and I gave in.
The report **argues convincingly that** tourism brings the island more money than problems.
items.watchOut: Переконливо — convincingly або persuasively, а не persuadingly чи convincedly: так майже не кажуть. Argue тут — «доводити», а argue with sb — «сперечатися, сваритися з кимось».

items.pattern: draw (sb's) attention to sth · draw attention away from sth · also call / bring attention to sth
items.meaning: make people notice something
items.example: The report **draws attention to** the lack of bike racks at the station.
more: The campaign **drew attention to** how much plastic ends up on our beaches.
Can I **draw your attention to** the fire exits at the back of the hall?
items.watchOut: «Привернути увагу до чогось» — draw attention to, а не pull attention to. Attract attention зазвичай кажуть, коли щось привертає увагу до себе: The street musician attracted a lot of attention. Pay attention to — звертати увагу самому, а draw attention to — змусити помітити інших.

items.pattern: (recent / new) research suggests / shows that… · research into / on sth · do / carry out research
items.meaning: studies give a good reason to believe something, though they don't prove it completely
items.example: **Research suggests** that children who walk to school concentrate better in class.
more: Recent **research suggests** that a short walk after dinner helps you sleep.
New **research suggests** that tourists spend more in small family shops than in big chains.
items.watchOut: Research зазвичай незлічуване: research suggests, а не researches suggest. Одне дослідження — a study або a piece of research. Suggest тут — «свідчити, наводити на думку», а не «пропонувати».

items.pattern: briefly summarise sth · summarise sth briefly · a brief summary
items.meaning: give the main ideas in a short, clear form
items.example: Before the vote, the club chairwoman **briefly summarised** the arguments for and against raising the fees.
more: At the end of each chapter, the author **briefly summarises** the main points.
Could you **briefly summarise** what the doctor said? I missed the start.
items.watchOut: «Коротко» — briefly, а не shortly: shortly означає «незабаром» (The train will arrive shortly). Британський правопис — summarise, американський — summarize. «Резюмувати» — не resume: resume означає «продовжити після перерви».

items.pattern: disagree profoundly / strongly / completely with sb/sth · disagree about / on a subject
items.meaning: disagree very strongly
items.example: I **disagree profoundly** with the idea that older people can't learn new things.
more: Many residents **disagree profoundly** with the plan to build flats on the playing fields.
The two writers **disagree profoundly** about the value of zoos.
items.watchOut: Підсилювач — profoundly, strongly або completely, а не highly. Не кажи I'm not agree: правильно I disagree або I don't agree. Прийменник: disagree with sb/sth, але disagree about / on a subject.

items.pattern: draw a conclusion / the conclusion that… · draw conclusions from sth · also come to / reach a conclusion
items.meaning: decide what is true after thinking about the facts
items.example: From the survey, we can **draw the conclusion that** most shoppers want longer opening hours.
more: You can't **draw conclusions** from one rainy week: the summer has only just started.
The doctor looked at my test results and **drew the conclusion that** I needed more vitamin D.
items.watchOut: «Робити висновок» — draw a conclusion, come to або reach a conclusion, а не make / do a conclusion: make тут — найпоширеніша калька. «На завершення» в кінці твору — In conclusion.

warmup.uk: Які висновки ви зробили після поїздки?
warmup.q: What conclusions did you ___ from the trip?
warmup.explain: Робити висновок — draw a conclusion (або come to / reach a conclusion). Make a conclusion — калька.

warmup.uk: Плануючи похід, треба брати до уваги погоду.
warmup.q: When you plan a hike, you have to take the weather into ___.
warmup.explain: Брати до уваги — take into consideration або take into account. «До уваги» тут не attention.

warmup.uk: Рішення закрити сільську бібліотеку порушує серйозні питання.
warmup.q: The decision to close the village library ___ serious questions.
warmup.explain: Порушувати питання — raise questions. Rise (підніматися) і arise (виникати) не мають додатка.

warmup.uk: Наша вчителька завжди робить наголос на правописі.
warmup.q: Our teacher always ___ emphasis on spelling.
warmup.explain: Робити наголос на — lay / put / place emphasis on. Make emphasis — калька.

warmup.uk: Автор проводить аналогію між сімейним бюджетом і бюджетом країни.
warmup.q: The author ___ an analogy between a family budget and a country's budget.
warmup.explain: Проводити аналогію (паралелі, межу) — draw an analogy (parallels, a distinction). Conduct — проводити захід чи дослідження.

warmup.uk: У листі до редакції авторка чітко висловлює свою думку про нову парковку.
warmup.q: In her letter to the editor, the writer clearly ___ her opinion about the new car park.
warmup.explain: Висловити думку — state / give / express your opinion. Tell і speak з opinion не поєднують.

warmup.uk: В останньому абзаці коротко підсумуйте головні аргументи.
warmup.q: In the last paragraph, ___ summarise the main arguments.

warmup.uk: Вона навела переконливі аргументи на користь безкоштовних уроків плавання для дітей.
warmup.q: She ___ a strong case for free swimming lessons for children.
warmup.explain: Наводити аргументи на користь — make a case for. Do a case — помилка.

A.q: Problems with our old flat ___ into two categories: noise and damp.
A.explain: Fall into categories — поділятися на категорії.

A.q: The doctor ___ no reference to the side effects of the medicine.
A.explain: Make (no) reference to — (не) згадувати, (не) посилатися на.

A.q: The leaflet ___ on issues such as noise, but doesn't discuss them in detail.
A.explain: Touch on issues — побіжно торкнутися питань, не розглядаючи їх докладно.

B.q: The town council wants to ___ the significance of tourism for local jobs.
B.explain: Assess the significance of — оцінити значення (важливість) чогось. Value — цінувати.

B.q: The guidebook lays special emphasis ___ cheap places to eat.
B.explain: Lay emphasis on — наголошувати на чомусь. Прийменник — on.

B.q: These figures ___ support to the view that people are eating less meat.
B.explain: Lend support to — підкріплювати думку. Lend тут — «надавати», а не «позичати».

C.q: The author ___ parallels between the two fishing villages.
In her new book, the travel writer ___ the position that hotels should pay a tourist tax.
C.explain: Adopt (take up) a position — зайняти позицію. Adapt — пристосовувати; occupy a position — обіймати посаду.

C.q: She argues ___ that the old cinema should be saved, and most readers agree with her.
C.explain: Argue convincingly — переконливо аргументувати. Persuadingly майже не вживають; profoundly поєднується з disagree.

The exhibition ___ parallels between life in the town a hundred years ago and life today.

At the start of the debate, each team has five minutes to ___ the case for its side.

example.title: My essay on school meals
example.uk:
Минулого місяця вчителька попросила нас написати твір про шкільне харчування. Я вирішив зайняти таку позицію: кожна дитина повинна отримувати безкоштовний гарячий обід.

Спочатку я провів чітку межу між дешевою їжею і здоровою. Потім я послався на опитування з нашої місцевої лікарні. Дослідження свідчать, що діти, які повноцінно обідають, краще зосереджуються на уроках, і опитування підкріпило цю думку. Я також побіжно торкнувся теми вартості, бо знав, що вона викличе запитання.

В останньому абзаці я коротко підсумував свої аргументи і зробив висновок, що безкоштовні обіди варті цих грошей. Учителька сказала, що я аргументував переконливо, але мій брат, який обожнює брати обід із собою, категорично не погодився!
example.en:
Last month our teacher asked us to write an essay about school meals. I decided to [[take up the position|c5]] that every child should get a free hot lunch.

First, I [[drew a clear distinction between|a2]] cheap food and healthy food. Then I [[made reference to|a4]] a survey from our local hospital.
